rule_field_policy: signals hold only facts read in the cited official document (vendor API reference, vendor's own SDK or spec repository, vendor network page, or the git project's protocol document).
Anything inferred, unread or opaque (a URL returned at run time) is in notes or not_separable, never in signals.

client_scope 'api' means the rule describes the vendor's public API (SDKs, scripts, integrations, automation). It is not evidence about the vendor's own web or desktop client, whose paths are unpublished for every service here.
Paths use {name} for a variable segment. path_exact must equal the path (query excluded), path_prefix must start it, path_pattern matches segment by segment.
A credential or opaque id in a path (bot token, webhook token, file id) is matched by shape and never emitted (AGENTS.md: no payloads, credentials or opaque identifiers as identity).
Precedence inside a parent: the most specific child wins (more signal fields matched); base is the fallback.
visibility: Every path, method and content-type signal needs Culvert's TLS decryption. In the visibility-only phase (research/README.md) the detector sees SNI, offered ALPN and port, so only the base children and host-only facts apply there.
